title: Finite modules descend from an element localization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $f\in R$, and let $R_f$ be the localization of $R$ at $f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Let $L$ be a finitely generated $R_f$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then there are a finitely generated $R$-module $M$ and an isomorphism of $R_f$-modules $M_f\cong L$, where $M_f$ is the localization of $M$ at the multiplicative set $\{1,f,f^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization].

source.place: Tag 05N5 (algebra-lemma-construct-fp-module), clause (1), line 31490; specialize the multiplicative set to powers of f and I=0

proof.text: Choose generators $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n$ of the finitely generated $R_f$-module $L$. They define a surjective $R_f$-linear map $q:R_f^{\oplus n}\to L$ sending the $i$-th standard basis vector to $\ell_i$. Let $\pi:R^{\oplus n}\to R_f^{\oplus n}$ be the localization map and put $K=\ker(q\circ\pi)$. This is the inverse-image construction in Tag 05N5, clause (1).

Set $M=R^{\oplus n}/K$. The images of the standard basis vectors generate $M$ as an $R$-module, so $M$ is finitely generated by the definition [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The map $R^{\oplus n}\to L$ given by $q\circ\pi$ kills $K$ and therefore induces an $R$-linear map $\bar q:M\to L$.

Because $f$ acts invertibly on the $R_f$-module $L$, the map $\bar q$ extends by the fraction formula to an $R_f$-linear map $\theta:M_f\to L$, $\theta((x+K)/f^r)=q(x/f^r)$. It is surjective: every element of $L$ is $q(x/f^r)$ for some $x$ and $r$, since $q$ is surjective and every vector in $R_f^{\oplus n}$ has such a representative. It is injective: if $\theta((x+K)/f^r)=0$, multiplication by the unit $f^r$ gives $q(x/1)=0$, so $x\in K$ and the localized class is zero. Thus $\theta$ is the required isomorphism $M_f\cong L$. This is exactly the conclusion of Tag 05N5, clause (1), after taking $I=0$ and $S=\{1,f,f^2,\ldots\}$.
